videos.title: En bra känsla för alla slag. Alltid från bakre höft till främre axel…
videos.channel: Bättre & Enklare golf med Marcus Edblad PGA
videos.summary_source_text:
En bra känsla för alla slag. Alltid från bakre höft till främre axel… Att svinga från bakre höft till främre axel ger oss väldigt många fördelar och en otroligt skön känsla i slagen.

Vi behöver rotera för att hjälpa våra händer förflytta sig men allt annan rotation är bortkastad energi.

#golf #golftips #golfswing 

0:00 Intro till så här ska det kännas

Nu finns det möjlighet att genom appen Skillest göra mig till din personliga tränare. Du hittar mig på denna länk: https://skillest.com/app/profile/marcus-edblad

Låt mig hjälpa dig finna bättre slag, bollträff, riktning och svinghastighet. Oavsett om du slår en wedge, järnklubba eller driver kan du med dina händer lära dig golfslag som du inte trodde var möjliga. Längre och rakare slag kräver alltid träning men något alla kan lära sig.  

Vare sig du kämpar med en slice eller en hook så har jag videos som kan guida till bättre golf. Är du nybörjare så kan du börja med min grönt kort eller nybörjarkurs.

Försök ersätta dåliga vanor med nya bättre vanor. Oavsett vilket loft eller skaft din klubba har så är det du som bestämmer vad som ska hända. Oavsett om det står callaway, ping, titleist eller taylor made på klubban så kan du slå bra slag.

Var noga med vad du tittar på. Det finns många duktiga instruktörer på nätet, några av mina favoriter är Mike Malaska, Mike Dunaway, Mike Austin.

Försök fokusera på grunderna i slaget bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår. Träna med fördel på en sak i taget. Tränar du din svinghastighet måste du tillåta att det går snett och tränar du raka slag kan du inte samtidigt svinga i max fart.

Ha tålamod och låt det ta sin tid, luras inte av genvägar som bara gör att du tappar fokus från det viktiga. Golf kommer alltid vara svårt men vi kan med träning se till att vi blir bättre för varje dag som går.

Titta mycket på golf på TV. Bryson Dechambeu, Dustin Johnson, Rory Mcilroy kan inspirera till längre slag och andra som Tiger Woods, Viktor Hovland, Ludvig Åberg och Phil Mickelson kan ge dig fantasi att skapa nya slag.

Träna styrketräning för hela kroppen för att må bra genom livet och skapa en effektiv maskin. Träna händer, handleder och armar för att skapa en effektiv release och mer svinghastighet.

Du kan finna inspiration i filmer som Happy Gilmore, Tin Cup eller Bagger Vance. Filmer som Rocky kan ge dig motivation att ta dig till gymet. Legender som Arnold Schwarzenegger, Sylvester Stallone eller Hulk Hogan kan få dig att vilja bli starkare och Moe Norman, Arnold Palmer, Ben Hogan, Sam Snead eller Jack Nicklaus kan inspirera dig att bli en bättre golfare. 

Ge aldrig upp i sökandet och träningen för att få bästa bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår.

Filmat med iPhone 17 och redigerat i iMovie på en Macbook. Att svinga från bakre höft till främre axel ger oss väldigt många fördelar och en otroligt skön känsla i slagen.

Vi behöver rotera för att hjälpa våra händer förflytta sig men allt annan rotation är bortkastad energi.

videos.summary_source_text:
Cameron Young SURGES with record-tying 61 | Round 2 | Rocket Classic | 2026 In the second round of the 2026 Rocket Classic, Cameron Young shot 9-under 61 to surge up the leaderboard at 10-under overall. 

The PGA TOUR heads to Detroit this week for the Rocket Classic, the penultimate event of the 2026 Regular Season, with FedExCup Playoff places still up for grabs. Detroit Golf Club also unveils its extensive $16 million renovation for the first time, providing a fresh challenge as players make one final push before the postseason. Fresh off his breakthrough victory at the 3M Open, 21-year-old Jackson Koivun returns looking to build on his rapid rise after climbing into the FedExCup's top 70. World No. 3 Cameron Young leads the field alongside recent three-time winner Chris Gotterup, while Wyndham Clark arrives in excellent form following an impressive summer that included his second U.S. Open title. Defending champion Aldrich Potgieter also returns, aiming to become the first player to successfully defend the Rocket Classic. The field is further strengthened by Russell Henley, Xander Schauffele, J.J. Spaun, Si Woo Kim and Akshay Bhatia, while Jordan Spieth and Brooks Koepka are both set to make their tournament debuts. With just one week remaining before the FedExCup Playoffs begin, every point carries added significance for those looking to extend their seasons. With 500 FedExCup points on offer and the Playoff race reaching its climax, the Rocket Classic promises another pivotal week as the PGA TOUR Regular Season enters its final stretch.

It Takes This Kind Of Confidence To Change Your Angle The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

The Curious Case of the Carolina Hurricanes and Jesperi Kotkaniemi As we're now 60 days from Opening Night for the Carolina Hurricanes, what is the plan with the roster? With Seth Jarvis expecting to miss 4 to 6 months, who will replace him in the interim? Could it be Bradly Nadeau, who has shown promise and deserves a longer look? Or is it Jesperi Kotkaniemi, who's been with the team since 2021-22? He's had his chances, but after last season, has it run its course? On the Friday Edition of Locked On Hurricanes,  Zach begins the show by sharing his thoughts on the case of how Kotkaniemi has still not found his role within the Hurricanes' system. He has shown flashes of being someone who can be a defensive center, but doesn't show the physicality enough. Plus, with how he only played 42 games in the regular season and none in the playoffs, has the ship sailed on the Finnish forward? Secondly, Zach shares his thoughts on how Nadeau has proven he could be used more often this upcoming season for the Hurricanes. After scoring three goals in 12 games, along with his play with the Chicago Wolves, how much more does he need to do? Finally, Zach concludes the show by sharing his thoughts on who should start more while Jarvis is out. Is it Kotkaneimi, or Nadeau? All of that and more, on the latest edition of Locked On Hurricanes.

videos.summary_source_text:
Pulled Iron Shots Comment "fix me" and I'll send you the fix to this pesky problem!

Stop blaming your clubface, your right shoulder could be causing BOTH of your worst iron misses. 👀🏌️‍♂️
When your right shoulder moves out toward the ball, it sends your swing path left. From there, you’ll usually see one of two shots:
❌ A solid iron shot that pulls hard left
❌ A weak, floating slice that loses 30–40 yards

The key is learning how to use your right shoulder properly so you can rotate through the ball confidently—without worrying about the dreaded left miss.

Which one shows up more in your golf swing: the pull left or the weak slice right? Comment below! 👇

videos.title: One feel for every swing from pith to driver…
videos.channel: Better & Easier golf with your guide Marcus Edblad
videos.summary_source_text:
One feel for every swing from pith to driver… If I could give you one feeling for every shot this is it. Always swing from trail hip to lead shoulder.

#golfswing #golf #golftips 

Online lesson are now a possibility on Skillest: https://skillest.com/app/profile/marcus-edblad

0:00 Intro to how to feel an effortless golf swing. 

Let me help you get an effortless golfswing with speed, distance and accuracy. I call it the circle of speed. A good release will help you to a better impact and longer drives and irons without slice and hook. How to swing a golf club need to be adjusted to your skill level and experience. 

Long and straight is the goal for everyone but it takes time. Try to focus on one thing not everything when you practise. Impact, face control and swingpath will always be the most important part to drill. We focus too much on rotation but no good golf shot will be executed just by rotating. 

We also need to understand that many myths in golf are misleading. Everything that you find on the internet isn’t true. Ben Hogan, Sam Snead are two of the legends that are often misunderstood.  To understand golf we need to take it step by step and learn every part of the swing before we move on to the next. It's like a big jigsaw puzzle that we all can figure out. 

A will never call a slice sexy but a high draw is beautiful in a very special way. Some pro's that hit draw: Rory McIroy, Xander Schauffele, Patrick Reed, Sepp Straka, Bryson Dechambeau  and many, many more. 

We shall not keep our head still, only start with the hips, look only at the ball or keep the left or right arm straight. Understand what do do with the club and let your body find the best way possible. 

This is not Rick Shiels, Saguto golf, Danny Maude, Meandmygolf, the Average Golfer, Malaska, Mark Crossfield, Alex Elliot Golf or Paige Spiranac. This is a method that anyone can learn if you give it a chance. 

If you use callaway, ping, titleist, takomo or taylor made clubs doesn’t matter you can learn to hit good golf shots. Your loft or your shaft on the club will not change but you can always get better. 

Find what inspires you. Golf basics are the same for everyone. The pga tour, longdrivers or other good golfers can all help you find better golf shots. Watch what they do instead of listed to what they say. Listen mostly to your body and figure out what you need to do to produce the same results as the pros on TV. Be careful when you watch a golf swing in slow motion. The result isn't always what the golfer is trying to do. Feel and real are seldom the same. 

We can find inspiration in a lot of things. You can find training motivation watching movies like Rocky, Tin Cup or Happy Gilmore and find mental inspiration in legends like Arnold Schwarzenegger, Hulk Hogan, Sylvester Stallone or Mike Tyson. Maybe we sometimes need to hear about crazy achievements from people like David Goggins, Jocko Willink, Ct Fletcher, Jim Rohn or Tony Robbins. 

Mike Malaska, Mike Austin, Mike Dunaway, Pete Cowen and Steve Pratt are some of my favorite golf instructors online. Find the tips that make your golf better. Decide what you want to hit. I teach a draw but many like a fade and nobody likes a hook or slice. 

Your hips or your lag is not the key to golf. Your hands will decide the shot and you can do like Tiger Woods and trust your hands. Teach your hands to hit different shots. Hit big hooks and slices to understand what happens. Only straight is not gonna teach you anything. 

Bryson Dechambeu and Kyle Birkshire can inspire you to hit it longer. Tiger Woods and Phil Mickelson can give you inspiration and motivation to test new things and new golf shots. Linn Grant, Viktor Hovland and Ludvig Aberg can show you the future of golf. 

The Masters, Players Championship, The Players, The Open and US Open can make you love golf even more. See the best in the world solve all the problems we all need to master any golf course. Golf is a craft and you need fantasy, feel and skills to master it.

Questions my videos will answer:

How to swing faster. How to hit longer. How to swing faster. How to hit your irons better. How to be better at anything. How to master the circle of speed. How to get a better short game. How to hit your wedge better. How to release the golf club. How to rotate in golf. Best tips for beginner golfers. How to hit down on the ball. How to hit up on the ball. How to rotate hips in the golf swing. How to hit straight every time. How to stop slicing. How to swing effortlessly.

videos.summary_source_text:
Still slicing your driver? Check your right elbow Still slicing your driver? Check your right elbow 👀

If the tip of your right elbow never gets in front of your shirt seam during the downswing, your hips and shoulders may spin open—sending the club across the ball and straight into “sliced city.” 🏌️‍♂️➡️
Try this instead: let your arms drop, tuck your right elbow just in front of your shirt seam, and allow the club to shallow behind you. This helps you approach the ball from the inside so you can hit straighter drives, create a draw, and find more fairways.

The Blue Brick makes this drill even more effective by giving you instant feedback when you spin out or come over the top.

Strength Training: Best or Worst Trend in 2026? Strength Training: Best or Worst Trend?

Strength training is crucial for aging well. It’s crucial for bone health, metabolic balance, hormones and even brain health. 

But there's a catch.

Many people focus only on strength while neglecting cardio and mobility. That's a mistake. 

Our data also shows that most students over 40 have at least two sedentary days every week (less than 5K steps). 

That’s not good. 

You don't need to become a hybrid athlete or spend hours training every day. You just need a balanced routine that includes three essentials: strength, cardio, and mobility. Strength Training: Best or Worst Trend?

In this candid post-round walkthrough, Dalke offers an honest look at the highs, lows, and mindset of competing on the PGA TOUR. 

The PGA TOUR heads to Detroit this week for the Rocket Classic, the penultimate event of the 2026 Regular Season, with FedExCup Playoff places still up for grabs. Detroit Golf Club also unveils its extensive $16 million renovation for the first time, providing a fresh challenge as players make one final push before the postseason. Fresh off his breakthrough victory at the 3M Open, 21-year-old Jackson Koivun returns looking to build on his rapid rise after climbing into the FedExCup's top 70. World No. 3 Cameron Young leads the field alongside recent three-time winner Chris Gotterup, while Wyndham Clark arrives in excellent form following an impressive summer that included his second U.S. Open title. Defending champion Aldrich Potgieter also returns, aiming to become the first player to successfully defend the Rocket Classic. The field is further strengthened by Russell Henley, Xander Schauffele, J.J. Spaun, Si Woo Kim and Akshay Bhatia, while Jordan Spieth and Brooks Koepka are both set to make their tournament debuts. With just one week remaining before the FedExCup Playoffs begin, every point carries added significance for those looking to extend their seasons. With 500 FedExCup points on offer and the Playoff race reaching its climax, the Rocket Classic promises another pivotal week as the PGA TOUR Regular Season enters its final stretch.

Why Pagani BOLTS cost more than a Porsche 911! Mat’s flown over to Modena in Italy to visit the Pagani factory. He’ll start off with a visit to the museum, seeing some of the earlier models and Pagani creations. After that, he’ll visit the factory for a personalised tour with Horacio Pagani. 

Explore new and used cars with Carwow: https://bit.ly/Change-Your-Car-3007

It’s time for an all-access tour of the Pagani factory! 

Mat’s over in Modena, Italy, and he’s about to see just what goes into creating some of the rarest and most expensive cars in the world! 

First up, he’s going to see what led Horacio Pagani to where he is today, with a trip to the Pagani museum. He’ll look over some of his first creations, including a bike and a Formula 2 car, while also getting up close with some of the first Paganis ever created. 

After that, it's time for the factory tour. Mat will join up with Horacio for a look around the factory, but this is no normal car factory! There are no long production lines or a huge workforce. There are only 300 employees in total, and every car is hand-assembled by a small team. Every car has its place in the factory, where it stays during the 9 week build process. This means every element, even down to the tiniest detail, has 100% traceability. 

With only 67 cars made in the last 12 months, it shows just how much detail goes into each car. The question is, what’s your favourite Pagani? Let us know in the comments! Buffalo Sabres Are Back In The Spotlight After 14 Years Of Playoff Purgatory | DLLS Stars Podcast Become a DIEHARD! alldlls.com/diehard

The Other 31: Buffalo Sabres
Our guest today is Joe Yerdon, Buffalo Sabres beat writer for Noted Hockey and Bleacher Report. The Sabres ended a 14-year playoff drought in 2025-26, but they did so in the most dramatic way possible. On December 8, 2025, Buffalo was in last place in the Eastern Conference and ranked 30th overall in NHL, with a record of 11-14-4 (26 pts., 0.448) in 29 games. In short, they looked destined to miss the post season for a 15th consecutive campaign. Suddenly, they flipped a switch. The Sabres rattled off a 10-game winning streak, tying a franchise record, and igniting an incredible run of 39-9-5 (83 pts., 0.783) over their final 53 games of the regular season, which was the best record in the league over that span. They won the Atlantic Division, beat the Boston Bruins in six games in the first round and they lost a thrilling seven-game series against the Montréal Canadiens in the second round, punctuated by Alex Newhook’s Game 7 series-clinching goal in overtime at KeyBank Center. Suddenly relevant again, the Sabres have been busy in the offseason, including trading away Alex Tuch and Bowen Byram.

30.07.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

videos.title: A Behind The Scenes Look At Getting Drafted To The Rockies with Tanner Sagouspe | GS Exclusive
videos.summary_source_text:
A Behind The Scenes Look At Getting Drafted To The Rockies with Tanner Sagouspe | GS Exclusive Join us for a must-watch exclusive interview with Rockies prospect and rising baseball start, Tanner Sagouspe!Tanner was recently selected 254th overall in the ninth round of the 2026 MLB Draft by the Colorado Rockies, marking a huge milestone in his baseball career. A California native from Fresno, Tanner spent his childhood playing baseball and growing a love for the game. After an impressive high school career, Tanner committed to play college baseball at Cal Poly, San Luis Obispo.

Tanner entered his collegiate career as an outfielder and hitter, but an injury quickly changed the direction of his path. After redshirting his freshman year due to injury, Tanner moved around the diamond, trying to find the position where he could thrive the most. After several different opportunities, including returning to the outfield and even catching, Tanner ultimately decided to focus on pitching. For the remainder of his time at Cal Poly, he developed into the consistent closer for the Mustangs, posting impressive numbers and making major strides on the mound.

With one more year of college eligibility and hoping to someday get the call that every player dreams of in July, Tanner attended graduate school at Texas Christian University and pitched for the Horned Frogs in the Big 12. While in Fort Worth, Tanner continued refining his pitching arsenal and worked to position himself as a standout prospect heading into the MLB Draft.

Now, fast forward to July 2026, where after a remarkable journey and a whirlwind of emotions, Tanner was selected by the Colorado Rockies — an unforgettable moment that he’ll never forget.

Mark Robinson sits down with Tanner to discuss his journey as a collegiate player, the emotions leading up to hearing his name called on draft day, and what comes next now that he is officially part of the Rockies organization. From draft day stories and full-circle moments to an inside look at how a brand-new draft class begins preparing for professional baseball, you won’t want to miss this exclusive interview with one of the newest members of the Colorado Rockies organization, Tanner Sagouspe!

Title:3 Easy Ways to Add Driver Distance #golfswing #golftips Here are three straightforward ways to add more distance with your driver. Start by flaring your lead foot and moving the ball farther forward in your stance, which helps you rotate better and hit up on the ball. Next, create a slight tilt away from the target at address to set up the proper launch conditions. Finally, feel more width at the top of the backswing by getting the hands further away from you. These three changes work together to help you hit it longer with more consistency.

Rickie Fowler opens with 7-under 63 in Detroit | Round 1 | Rocket Classic | 2026 In the first round of the Rocket Classic, 2023 champion Rickie Fowler goes low with a 7-under 63 to sit two back of the lead.

The PGA TOUR heads to Detroit this week for the Rocket Classic, the penultimate event of the 2026 Regular Season, with FedExCup Playoff places still up for grabs. Detroit Golf Club also unveils its extensive $16 million renovation for the first time, providing a fresh challenge as players make one final push before the postseason. Fresh off his breakthrough victory at the 3M Open, 21-year-old Jackson Koivun returns looking to build on his rapid rise after climbing into the FedExCup's top 70. World No. 3 Cameron Young leads the field alongside recent three-time winner Chris Gotterup, while Wyndham Clark arrives in excellent form following an impressive summer that included his second U.S. Open title. Defending champion Aldrich Potgieter also returns, aiming to become the first player to successfully defend the Rocket Classic. The field is further strengthened by Russell Henley, Xander Schauffele, J.J. Spaun, Si Woo Kim and Akshay Bhatia, while Jordan Spieth and Brooks Koepka are both set to make their tournament debuts. With just one week remaining before the FedExCup Playoffs begin, every point carries added significance for those looking to extend their seasons. With 500 FedExCup points on offer and the Playoff race reaching its climax, the Rocket Classic promises another pivotal week as the PGA TOUR Regular Season enters its final stretch.

videos.title: Three Rare Skating Habits From Connor McDavid
videos.summary_source_text:
Three Rare Skating Habits From Connor McDavid The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains how proper hydration and certain natural drinks and foods may support normal kidney function, urinary health, circulation, and the body’s ability to remove waste. You will learn about water, lemon, cranberry, beets, ginger, turmeric, celery, parsley, dandelion, watermelon, garlic, and apple cider vinegar, along with the everyday habits that can place extra stress on your kidneys, including too much salt, processed food, excess sugar, smoking, alcohol, dehydration, and overuse of certain pain medications. These natural choices are not a substitute for medical treatment, and anyone with kidney disease, diabetes, heart problems, kidney stones, or fluid or potassium restrictions should speak with a healthcare professional before making major dietary changes. videos.summary_source_text:
Episode 53: Player Debates & Off-Season Updates | Tri-State Hockey Podcast Jonny Lazarus, Arthur Staple and Mike Rupp are back for Episode 53 of the Tri-State Hockey Podcast to break down the biggest storylines surrounding the New Jersey Devils, New York Rangers and New York Islanders as the NHL offseason continues.

The guys open the show by discussing Vincent Trocheck's recent comments about choosing the Rangers because of Artemi Panarin, leading to a conversation about whether New York still has the star power to attract elite free agents. They examine Chris Drury's offseason, the perception surrounding the Rangers organization, and what the franchise must do to become a destination again.

The conversation then shifts to a debate over the NHL's best center duos after a recent ranking left both the Rangers and Islanders outside the top tiers. The crew explains why Jack Hughes and Nico Hischier deserve to be among the league's elite pairings, compares Mika Zibanejad and J.T. Miller against Bo Horvat and Mathew Barzal, and discusses where each Tri-State team stacks up down the middle.

Later, the guys answer listener questions, including what the Islanders need from Brayden Schenn and Ondřej Palát to justify last season's trade deadline moves, whether Bo Horvat or Mathew Barzal is more valuable moving forward, and if Dawson Mercer should already be locked into a long-term extension with the Devils.

Finally, they discuss the NHL's rising salary cap, how the next wave of superstar contracts could reshape the league, and which teams are best positioned for long-term success before wrapping up the show with their Bet365 Bet of the Day and final thoughts.

videos.title: The Most Capable Humanoid Robot Yet!
videos.summary_source_text:
The Most Capable Humanoid Robot Yet! Google just released Gemini Robotics 2 today, and it's a much bigger leap than you may think.

Unlike previous models, it coordinates everything from feet to fingertips, allowing the robot to balance and walk while handling delicate objects.

With 22 degrees of movement in its hands, it can seal Ziploc bags, unscrew lightbulbs, and even tie trash bag knots.

Plus, an on-device version runs locally without an internet connection and can adapt to new robot bodies in just a few hours.

To be clear: this new release "Google Robotics 2" is the AI software behind the robot, not a physical robot you buy directly from Google. It powers hardware from partners like Apptronik on their Apollo 2 robot. 

For Developers: You can access the reasoning model "Gemini Robotics ER 2" today on Google AI Studio.
For Hardware Integrators: The full Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and On-Device models are currently available to partners through Google DeepMind's early access program.

videos.summary_source_text:
Buzz Huddle Test: 4 Humans, 2 AI Agents 🔗 Free Buzz community: https://mrc.fm/cmbuzz
🤖 This video was streamed live on X and edited into highlights by a Buzz AI agent using Fable so apologies for any wonky edits!

🎙️ The audio gets wobbly the moment the huddle starts.

Huddles are a very experimental feature.

My free community on Buzz hit 102 members, so I celebrated by opening a voice huddle and inviting whoever turned up. Four humans and two AI agents later, Grok and Claude Haiku, we had a real answer: it works, it is rough, and the interesting part is not the voice at all. Agents answer in text rather than speech, every reply spins up a full agent harness so the latency is brutal, and the participant list flickers between active and ended while people are clearly still talking. But the live transcript is quietly brilliant, with every line cryptographically signed and attributed to whoever said it, and by the end I had an agent summarise the entire session into something worth sending to the Buzz team. Huge thanks to Patrik, Rian and Mingo for testing this with me live. Come and join the next one, my free Buzz community is open to anyone: https://mrc.fm/cmbuzz

Frequent urination at night is often more than just a bladder or prostate problem. Many people produce one to two cups of urine overnight, and much of this fluid comes from what was consumed earlier in the day, not just before bed.

By age 80, nighttime urination affects most adults. One possible clue is fluid retention, which is often associated with elevated glucose and insulin rather than simply drinking too much water or eating too much salt. An edema test and a fasting insulin test can help identify underlying issues.

Gravity also plays a role. Fluid that accumulates in the legs during the day can return to the bloodstream while you sleep, increasing urine production overnight. Sleep apnea and certain medications can also contribute to frequent nighttime urination.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

Jordan Staal joins Daily Faceoff Live to reflect on the Carolina Hurricanes' Stanley Cup-winning season and the journey that led him there after nearly 15 years with the franchise.

Staal discusses sticking with Carolina through difficult seasons, why he believed the organization would eventually become a champion, and what it meant to finally lift the Stanley Cup as captain. He also shares what changed during the Hurricanes' championship run, the additions that helped push the team over the top, and why the group believes it can compete for another Stanley Cup next season.

The conversation also covers Staal's remarkable NHL longevity, evolving his game over more than 1,400 NHL games, life growing up in Thunder Bay, his brothers Eric and Marc, and what winning a second Stanley Cup means at this stage of his career.

If you're a Hurricanes fan or looking for insight into leadership, championship culture, and one of the NHL's most respected veterans, this is an interview you won't want to miss.

Does the New Celebrini Contract Impact the Makar Extension? Broncos Make the Avs Look Like Scrooges Macklin Celebrini’s record-breaking extension with the San Jose Sharks sends shockwaves through the NHL. With the young phenom set to become the league’s highest-paid player, what ripple effects will this have on future contracts—especially Cale Makar’s next deal with the Colorado Avalanche?

Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson break down Celebrini’s rapid ascent, debate whether such massive contracts for emerging stars are justified, and examine the impact of rising salaries on team building. videos.title: This Mobility Test Explains Your Swing  #golfswing #golftips
videos.summary_source_text:
This Mobility Test Explains Your Swing  #golfswing #golftips This simple 90/90 mobility test gives you a clear look at how your right arm should function in the golf swing. From a 5-iron posture, lift and rotate the arm until it matches your spine angle—if you can’t get there, your backswing is likely compensating by standing up or losing posture. That compensation often leads to poor ball striking and inconsistent contact. Your swing should reflect what your body can actually do, even if that means a shorter backswing.

Who deserves PGA TOUR Player of the Year? + Rocket Classic Preview | The Drop The Drop heads to Detroit for the 2026 Rocket Classic, where players will look to make a late-season final push to get into the FedExCup Playoffs. Hosts Matt Every and Jeff Eisenband blind rank and debate who they think should be the 2026 Player of the Year. The players they ranked are Wyndham Clark, Matt Fitzpatrick, Chris Gotterup, Scottie Scheffler and Cameron Young. The two also discuss PGA TOUR rookie Jackson Koivun after he got his first win in three starts as a pro. Every interviewed Si Woo Kim about his 2026 season, The Open and the first time they played together. We learn what players must do if they want to “Master Motown” in this week’s edition of Champion’s Hole, which is the 17th at Detroit Golf Club. Lastly, Notah Begay III is the recipient of this year’s Payne Stewart Award. He’s surprised by Payne Stewart’s son, Aaron, during a Golf Channel broadcast rehearsal, with the award.

50 Goal Scorer Level Deception The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Drink This 30 Minutes Before Bed to Stop Waking Up at Night | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Drink This 30 Minutes Before Bed to Stop Waking Up at Night | Dr. Mandell Drink this about 30 minutes before bed to support hydration, nighttime blood sugar balance, digestion, and a calmer nervous system so you may sleep more comfortably and wake up feeling better. In this video, I explain how a simple warm drink made with lemon, a tiny pinch of salt, and a small amount of honey may help reduce some of the stress signals that can contribute to waking during the night. This is not a sleeping pill, and it does not force your body to sleep. Instead, it supports normal hydration, mineral balance, digestion, and the body’s natural overnight repair processes. Many people may notice fewer nighttime awakenings, less morning heaviness or bloating, and clearer thinking when they wake up.

Ingredients:
1 to 1½ cups warm water
Juice of ½ fresh lemon, about 1 tablespoon
A very small pinch of salt, about 1/16 teaspoon
½ teaspoon honey

How to take it:

Mix all the ingredients together and drink it about 30 to 60 minutes before bed. Use warm water, not hot water. Do not add extra salt or honey, because more is not better. The honey is only being used in a very small amount, not as a sugary drink.

This drink may not be appropriate for everyone. Speak with your healthcare professional before trying it if you have diabetes, kidney disease, high blood pressure, reflux, or any condition that requires you to restrict sodium, sugar, or fluids.

Research References:

Cedernaes J, Huang W, Ramsey KM, et al. Transcriptional basis for rhythmic control of hunger and metabolism within the liver. Cell Metabolism. 2019;30(5):870–885. PMID: 31585058.

Van Cauter E, Polonsky KS, Scheen AJ. Roles of circadian rhythmicity and sleep in human glucose regulation. Endocrine Reviews. 1997;18(5):716–738. PMID: 9408742.

Rasmussen DD, Mitton DR, Green J, Puchalski S. Chronic daily ethanol and withdrawal: circadian rhythms of cortisol and temperature. Endocrinology. 2001;142(12):5329–5336. PMID: 11713225.

Hofmann AF. Bile acids, the good, the bad, and the ugly. News in Physiological Sciences. 1999;14:24–29. PMID: 11390824.

Brad Dalke Full Mic'd Up Range Session | 2026 Rocket Classic Watch YouTube-golfer Brad Dalke's full range session ahead of the 2026 Rocket Classic this week in Detroit, MI. This marks Dalke's first PGA TOUR event since 2017. 

The PGA TOUR heads to Detroit this week for the Rocket Classic, the penultimate event of the 2026 Regular Season, with FedExCup Playoff places still up for grabs. Detroit Golf Club also unveils its extensive $16 million renovation for the first time, providing a fresh challenge as players make one final push before the postseason. Fresh off his breakthrough victory at the 3M Open, 21-year-old Jackson Koivun returns looking to build on his rapid rise after climbing into the FedExCup's top 70. World No. 3 Cameron Young leads the field alongside recent three-time winner Chris Gotterup, while Wyndham Clark arrives in excellent form following an impressive summer that included his second U.S. Open title. Defending champion Aldrich Potgieter also returns, aiming to become the first player to successfully defend the Rocket Classic. The field is further strengthened by Russell Henley, Xander Schauffele, J.J. Spaun, Si Woo Kim and Akshay Bhatia, while Jordan Spieth and Brooks Koepka are both set to make their tournament debuts. With just one week remaining before the FedExCup Playoffs begin, every point carries added significance for those looking to extend their seasons. With 500 FedExCup points on offer and the Playoff race reaching its climax, the Rocket Classic promises another pivotal week as the PGA TOUR Regular Season enters its final stretch.

Place an alignment stick behind the ball and a head cover just in front — then focus on swinging under the stick and over the head cover. 
You’ll shallow the club naturally, improve your path, and start hitting up on the ball for better launch and distance.

BREAKING: Macklin Celebrini Signs $94 MILLION Extension! Did the Sharks Get a STEAL? 🚨 The San Jose Sharks have locked up franchise superstar Macklin Celebrini, signing the 20-year-old to a 5-year, $94 million contract extension carrying an $18.8 million AAV. We break down why this deal makes perfect sense for San Jose, how the Flyers' Leo Carlsson offer sheet may have influenced the number, and why this contract could end up looking like a bargain.

In this video we cover:
✅ Full breakdown of Macklin Celebrini's 5-year, $94 million extension
✅ Why the Sharks committed $18.8 million per season
✅ How the Leo Carlsson offer sheet helped shape the market
✅ Why Celebrini could already be worth even more after a 115-point season
✅ What this means for San Jose's future salary cap and Stanley Cup window

Celebrini still has one year remaining on his entry-level contract, meaning this extension won't kick in until the 2027-28 season. Did Mike Grier just make one of the smartest contracts in the NHL, or is $18.8 million too much? Let us know your thoughts in the comments!

Ollie Bearman: High Hopes With Haas & Ferrari  | F1 Beyond The Grid Podcast Ferrari discovered him, trained him and gave him a place in Formula 1 with Haas. Ollie Bearman dreams of driving for the Scuderia, but with Lewis Hamilton enjoying a revival and Charles Leclerc committed long-term, what does Bearman's future hold?

Speaking to Tom Clarkson, Ollie discusses what he still believes he can achieve with Haas, why this year’s results don’t reflect how much his driving has improved, and whether he’d ever leave the Ferrari family to pursue other options.

Ollie also talks about stepping up as a team leader this year, recalling the time he picked up the microphone and addressed the whole team after a few difficult races.

Plus, he explains why he was moved to tears after driving Ayrton Senna’s 1985 Lotus at Silverstone.

videos.title: Why Trying Harder Can Keep Your Body Stuck | Somatic Practice from Kyoto
videos.summary_source_text:
Why Trying Harder Can Keep Your Body Stuck | Somatic Practice from Kyoto What if your body does not need more force—but better conditions for learning?

In this video, filmed in the quiet countryside of Keihoku, Kyoto, I explore why tightness, bracing, shallow breathing, stiffness, and fear of movement can sometimes increase when we keep pushing, correcting, or trying harder.

You’ll also be guided through a short, gentle seated somatic movement exploration to notice how the same movement can feel different when approached with less effort, more support, and curiosity.

This is not about avoiding all effort or discomfort. It is about giving your nervous system enough safety to sense, explore, and discover new possibilities.

A quick note: the river beside us was much louder in the original recording than I realized, so I re-recorded the narration to make the message and movement guidance easier to hear. The video itself is from the original filming in Kyoto.

Move slowly, stay within a comfortable range, and rest whenever you need.

If you are tired of treating your body like a problem to solve, you can learn more about my guided course, Moving Freely in Your Body, here:
https://taroiwamoto.com/thecourse

This course is for thoughtful, self-aware adults who are ready to move beyond chasing relief, correcting their body, or piecing together random exercises — and begin learning a different relationship with their body through guided somatic movement.

If you’re newer to this work, start with my free somatic masterclass:
Move More Freely in Your Body
https://taro-iwamoto.thinkific.com/courses/masterclass

Read my book:
Your Body Is Not Broken: A Gentle Somatic Path to Moving with More Ease, Trust, and Freedom

A short Kindle book for anyone tired of trying to fix their body and wanting a gentler way to begin again.
https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GX363HMX

About Taro Iwamoto

I help self-aware adults who feel stuck in recurring pain, tension, bracing, or fear of movement — even after trying many approaches — discover a gentler somatic, nervous-system-based path toward more ease, trust, and freedom in their body.

My work is not about forcing the body to change, finding the perfect exercise, or diagnosing what is wrong.

It is about helping your body and nervous system experience support, safety, connection, and new possibilities through gentle somatic movement.

Broncos, Rockies Trade Deadline & CU Buffs Breakdown with Charles Johnson | After the Horn Colorado sports are heating up as the MLB Trade Deadline approaches and NFL training camp officially gets underway.

On this episode of After the Horn, Woody Paige, Tom Green, and special guest Charles Johnson break down whether the Colorado Rockies are finally ready to become aggressive sellers at the trade deadline, what the future holds for Hunter Goodman, Kyle Freeland and the franchise, and why this deadline could define the organization's new direction.

The crew also dives into the Denver Broncos as Sean Payton begins another training camp with Bo Nix, discusses Davis Webb's new role as offensive coordinator, the Jonathan Cooper situation, and what expectations should be for Denver entering the 2026 NFL season.

Charles Johnson also joins the show for an in-depth conversation about Deion Sanders, Julian Lewis, Colorado football, NIL, the transfer portal, and whether the Buffaloes are poised for a breakout season. Plus, Woody shares behind-the-scenes journalism stories, the panel discusses Kyle Shanahan's car accident, and plenty more from around the sports world.

Topics include:

Rockies MLB Trade Deadline strategy
Hunter Goodman & Kyle Freeland trade talk
Sean Payton and Broncos Training Camp
Bo Nix Year 2 expectations

What defines normal cholesterol levels today isn’t the same as it was decades ago. As the threshold for high cholesterol has continued to decrease, millions more people have been diagnosed. The focus has also shifted from total cholesterol to LDL cholesterol, but if cholesterol alone is the problem, why do cardiovascular disease rates remain so high?

Not all LDL cholesterol is the same. Small, dense LDL particles are associated with inflammation, while large, buoyant LDL particles behave differently. An advanced lipid profile can help distinguish between these two types.

Insulin resistance is one of the key drivers of high LDL cholesterol and is often linked to the chronic consumption of sugar and starches. A fasting insulin test may provide valuable insight into your metabolic health. Inflammation, low thyroid function, chronic stress, and fatty liver can also contribute to elevated LDL cholesterol.

Regarding the Carolina Hurricanes, which three players are on milestone watch heading into the upcoming season? On the Wednesday Edition of Locked On Hurricanes,  Zach begins the show by sharing his thoughts on the captain, Jordan Staal, and how he is not only on an NHL milestone watch but a Hurricanes milestone watch. Regarding the NHL, he is only 21 assists shy of 450 in his career, and three points shy of 750. When it comes to the Hurricanes, Staal is 28 games shy of 1,000 with the team, along with two goals from 200, and one point from 500. Heading into his 15th season with the Hurricanes and his 21st NHL season, Staal is in for a memorable season. Secondly, Sebastian Aho is 44 games shy of playing 800 in his career, all with the Hurricanes. While he did manage to reach 310 goals and 401 assists last season, he is only 40 goals shy of 350 and 49 assists shy of 450; can he achieve both in 2026-27? Furthermore, he is only 89 points shy of 800 in his career. Is he due for an 89- or 90-point season? Finally, Zach concludes the show by sharing his thoughts on how Nikolaj Ehlers is 44 games shy of 800 in his career. He is also 10 assists shy of 350, and nine points from 600 in his career. videos.title: New Audi Q9 - have they made a HUGE mistake?
videos.summary_source_text:
New Audi Q9 - have they made a HUGE mistake? The all-new Audi Q9 and SQ9 have been revealed. We’ll walk around the exterior design, interior design, discuss the engine options and reveal the price. 

Explore new and used car deals with Carwow: https://bit.ly/Change-Your-Car-2907

This is the all-new Audi Q9 and SQ9! 

It’s the largest production car Audi has ever produced, both in terms of length, height, and width! It’s an absolutely colossal 7-seater! 

The question is, does it do enough to appeal to those of you looking for a 7-seater when there are class-leaders like the Mercedes GLS and BMW X7 out there? Let’s take a closer look. 

In terms of the exterior design, Audi has made an effort to make the Q9 look like a truly premium product. Around the back, the panels are all smooth, with an embedded Audi logo across the middle, while there are also curved LED taillights on either side. Being so large, it has real presence from the side, with alloys available up to 23 inches in size! Up front, the Q9 comes with a vertical slated illuminating grille, while the SQ9 has a more sporty-styled one. Either way, they’re both absolutely massive, and they’re flanked by more LED headlights, just like at the back. 

On the inside, both the Q9 and SQ9 interiors are dominated by screens. There’s a large digital dial & infotainment screen, and as in all new Audis, there’s the option for a passenger screen as well. The screens are surrounded by quite a large bezel, but the infotainment system is pretty easy to use. Unfortunately, the quality and customisation of the dial screen seems to be worse than on previous cars! Elsewhere, the cabin is well-built, with soft-touch materials throughout, and the SQ9 comes with S-badging on the steering wheel, embossed on the headrests, and on the door sills. 

The range-topping SQ9 will come with a 4-litre twin-turbo V8 that can deliver 590hp and 800Nm to all four wheels! However, there’s a catch… Due to EU regulations, the V8 will only be available in America! For us in Europe, the SQ9 will only arrive with a 2.9-litre V6. 

The all-new Audi Q9 will start from around £100,000. But does it offer enough to sway you away from a Mercedes or BMW 7-seater? Stick with Mat to see for yourself!

28.07.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

videos.title: 3 Levels Of Stickhandling, How Far Can You Make It?
videos.summary_source_text:
3 Levels Of Stickhandling, How Far Can You Make It? The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Putt Like The Pros #golfswing #golftips
videos.summary_source_text:
Putt Like The Pros #golfswing #golftips Most amateur golfers end up ruining their tempo and distance control by trying to guide or overly control the club - accelerating through the ball and having too short of a backswing. On the other hand, pros have better and more consistent distance control because their tempo stays similar all the way through the ball and they take the club far enough back in their backswing. 
Once you feel the putter flow naturally, you’ll start rolling it the perfect distance far more often.

videos.title: Heart Attacks and Strokes Peak at This Time—Do This When You Wake Up | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Heart Attacks and Strokes Peak at This Time—Do This When You Wake Up | Dr. Mandell Heart attacks and strokes do not happen evenly throughout the day. Research has shown that the first few hours after waking can place greater stress on the heart and brain because blood pressure rises, stress hormones increase, blood vessels tighten, and platelets can become more active. This normal morning surge may become more concerning when it is combined with poor sleep, chronic stress, dehydration, inflammation, reduced circulation, or blood pressure that does not fall properly overnight.

In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains the physiology behind this morning danger window and why prevention often begins the night before. You will learn how sleep quality, late-night eating, alcohol, inactivity, heavy caffeine, and sudden morning stimulation may affect circulation and cardiovascular strain. You will also discover simple habits that can help your body move more gradually from sleep into the day, including slow breathing, gentle calf and hand movements, proper hydration, natural morning light, and avoiding unnecessary stress immediately after waking.

The goal of this video is not to create fear. It is to help you understand how your body responds during the morning hours and how small, consistent lifestyle changes may support healthier blood flow, more balanced blood pressure, and better long-term heart and brain health.

Always speak with your healthcare professional if you have high blood pressure, heart disease, circulation problems, a history of stroke, chest pain, unusual shortness of breath, sudden weakness, facial drooping, difficulty speaking, or any other concerning symptoms.

A protein dessert for a flat belly! LOW-CALORIE & SUGAR-FREE! A protein dessert for a flat belly! LOW-CALORIE & SUGAR-FREE! Healthy High-Protein Snack. This recipe is incredibly easy to make and absolutely delicious. A creamy vanilla cottage cheese dessert that’s so good, you’ll want to make it again and again. Save this recipe and give it a try!

1 tsp gelatin. ¼ cup (60 ml) water.
3 egg yolks.
½ cup (125 ml) milk. 1 tbsp stevia.
This dessert is high in protein and surprisingly low in calories.
Heat until very hot, but do not let it boil.
Melt the gelatin, but do not boil it.
1 cup (170 g) cottage cheese.
¼ tsp vanilla.
This delicious dessert comes together with just a few simple ingredients in only 5 minutes.
Place in the fridge for 2 hrs.
If desired, spread some melted sugar-free chocolate on top.

Mat’s got his hands on the all-new Mercedes C-Class Electric! 

It’s the first time the C-Class has gone electric, and he’s about to test it over in Helsinki and see just what it’s like to drive. Not only that, he’ll be seeing if it offers real value against class-leading competitors like the Tesla Model 3. 

So can this all-new EV compete with the best? Let’s take a closer look…

In terms of design, the new C-Class Electric uses three-pointed-star headlights and taillights, as seen in all recent Mercedes reveals. The car we have here is in AMG-Line trim, which means it comes with large front vents and lower front and rear bumpers. It’s also fitted with the Black Pack, which means the grille is blacked out, and there are black surrounds on the windows and the side skirts. It looks pretty smart overall, but the same can’t be said for the car without the Black Pack fitted - the grille looks absolutely awful! 

On the inside, the cabin is dominated by a large screen that stretches across the entire dash (although in the entry-level car, it’s effectively three screens rather than one). The infotainment system is crisp and easy to use, although there are lots of menus and the climate controls are handled through the screen. Elsewhere, the cabin is well-built with soft-touch materials throughout, although there are a few switches and features which are plastic and relatively cheap-feeling to touch.

The C-Class Electric comes with two motors, and these combine for a maximum output of 482hp and 800Nm. It comes with all-wheel drive, and can accelerate to 62mph in 4.1 seconds. It has a claimed range of 473 miles, and it comes with 300kW charging, which enables you to add 200 miles of range in just 10 minutes. 

The C-Class Electric has a starting price of £57,995 for the entry-level car, rising all the way to £70,995 for the top-of-the-range model. In contrast, a top-spec Tesla Model 3 costs just £59,990. So is the new Mercedes really worth it? You’ll need to stick with Mat to see for yourself!

27.07.26 - Ep.19 - The Rise of Capital Identity Welcome to Episode 19 of RIFT Before You Quit, where we explore one of the biggest shifts that could reshape the future of finance: Capital Identity.

For generations, financial opportunities have been based on one simple question: How much money do you have? But what if the future isn't about the size of your account, but about how well you manage your capital?

In this episode, we examine how AI, blockchain, behavioural analytics, and transparent financial infrastructure are creating a world where trust, consistency, discipline, and risk management could become more valuable than wealth itself.

You'll discover why financial reputation may soon become a portable digital asset that follows you throughout your investing and trading journey.

In this episode we cover:

- What Capital Identity is and why it matters
- Why traditional finance measures ownership instead of behaviour
- How AI could evaluate traders based on discipline instead of profits
- The rise of on-chain reputation systems
- Why behavioural data is becoming the new financial currency
- How institutions evaluate trust before allocating capital
- Why consistency often beats spectacular returns
- The evolution from execution-based finance to reputation-based finance
- How blockchain can create permanent, verifiable financial histories
- The concept of a future "Capital Passport"
- How Smart Money participation helps develop institutional thinking
- Why RIFT is being designed as participation infrastructure rather than simply another trading platform
- How behavioural history can eventually unlock larger financial opportunities
- The relationship between Smart Money, automated trading systems, reputation, and capital allocation
- Why future AI systems may analyse thousands of behavioural variables rather than focusing only on profitability
- How trust becomes measurable through data
- The future role of AI in evaluating risk, consistency, allocation, and long-term capital management

Throughout this episode, we continue building the long-term vision behind the RIFT ecosystem—not simply helping users become better traders, but helping them understand how professional capital is managed, protected, and allocated.

As discussed throughout this series, successful trading is not built on prediction alone. It is built on:

• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio allocation
• Consistency
• Discipline
• Long-term thinking

These are the qualities institutions value most, and they form the foundation of what may become tomorrow's financial identity.

Whether you're interested in trading, blockchain technology, AI, or simply understanding where modern financial infrastructure is heading, this episode offers valuable insight into one of the industry's most important emerging concepts.

Hindi - 27.07.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

Can Devon Toews prove last season’s dip was a blip, not a sign of age, and will Martin Necas finally shed his “playoff ghost” label? Uniform controversies, playoff disappointments, and a burning desire to reclaim Stanley Cup glory drive the debate: who on the Avalanche has the most to prove this year?

Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson break down the top Avs with pressure on their shoulders—spotlighting Logan O’Connor’s comeback from hip surgery, Scott Wedgewood’s need to replicate his breakout campaign, and Brock Nelson’s quest for redemption after a rough postseason. The Most Frustrating Part of Hockey The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body’s own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness.
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: The Golf Clubs That Sold Out in Minutes... Beat the "BEST" Ever?
videos.summary_source_text:
The Golf Clubs That Sold Out in Minutes... Beat the "BEST" Ever? Everyone called these golf clubs the BEST ever... then a new set arrived and sold out in minutes.

videos.summary_source_text:
Eat This for Better Circulation, Sharper Vision and Stronger Bones | Dr. Mandell Rainbow Swiss chard is one of the most colorful and nutrient-dense vegetables hiding in plain sight at the grocery store. Its deep-green leaves and brilliant red, yellow, orange, pink, and white stems provide a powerful combination of vitamin K, beta-carotene, vitamin C, magnesium, potassium, natural nitrates, fiber, lutein, zeaxanthin, betalains, flavonoids, and other beneficial plant compounds. These nutrients help support healthy circulation, normal blood pressure, eye health, bone strength, muscle and nerve function, digestion, regularity, and the body’s natural defenses against oxidative stress. In this video, I explain what the different colors represent, why every variety of Swiss chard can be nutritious, and how both the leaves and stems can be eaten. I’ll also show you a simple and delicious way to prepare it by cooking the colorful stems first, adding the leaves, and finishing everything with extra virgin olive oil, fresh garlic, lemon, and black pepper. Swiss chard is naturally high in vitamin K, so anyone taking warfarin should keep their intake consistent and speak with the healthcare professional monitoring their medication. It also contains oxalates, but most healthy people eating a normal portion as part of a varied diet do not need to fear this nutritious vegetable. People with a history of calcium-oxalate kidney stones who have been advised to limit oxalates may reduce some of the soluble oxalates by boiling the Swiss chard and discarding the cooking water. Whether you find rainbow, red, green, or traditional white-stemmed Swiss chard, this beautiful vegetable can be an easy and delicious way to add more protective color and valuable nutrition to your plate.

What 8 Hours at a Screen Does to Your Brain & Eyes What does 8 hours of screen time do to your eyes and brain? The effects can build hour by hour, impacting everything from blinking and focus to balance and peripheral vision.

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/44tPIyG

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements. 

What happens over time:
• Hour 1: The focusing muscles begin to tighten
• Hour 2: Blink rate drops and eye dryness can begin
• Hour 3: The eyes become locked into a static viewing pattern
• Hour 4: The retina receives far less light than it would outdoors
• Hour 5: The focusing muscles become less flexible
• Hour 6: Balance and spatial awareness may be affected
• Hour 7: Peripheral vision narrows
• Hour 8: Nearsightedness can begin to develop

If you only do one thing, step outside for 20 minutes each day without your phone and let your eyes naturally shift their focus between near and distant objects.

videos.summary_source_text:
Stop Doing Lunges Like This! (SAVE A FRIEND) FREE Total Body Program Here - http://athleanx.com/tbfree

The lunge is one of the top leg exercises you can include in your workouts, but it is also one of the exercises I see performed incorrectly every day. In this video, I am going to show you how to do lunges with proper form to build bigger quads, glutes, and hamstrings without unnecessarily beating up your knees. It is not just which exercises you do, but how you do them that matters most.

Step 1 of this lunge tutorial is choosing the right direction:

Most people automatically step forward when performing lunges. The problem is that the forward lunge can place more stress on the knee because the lead leg leaves the ground and has to absorb force when the foot lands. If your knees are irritated or you cannot control the landing, this can turn a great leg exercise into a painful one.

The reverse lunge is often the better option. By stepping backward, the working leg stays planted throughout the rep. This lets you control the movement while avoiding the abrupt loading that occurs when stepping forward. You still train the quads, glutes, and hamstrings, but with mechanics that are more comfortable and repeatable.

If you prefer forward lunges, consider walking lunges. Instead of stepping forward and then pushing backward, continue into the next rep. This improves the movement pattern, though it does not completely remove the extra stress when the lead foot hits the ground.

Step 2 of this lunge form guide is getting your foot placement right:

One of the most common lunge mistakes is stepping as though you are walking on a tightrope. When both feet remain directly in line, balance becomes the main challenge instead of building your legs. Step back and slightly out to create a wider base of support.

To determine how far back to step, reach with the toe of the back foot. Once the toe contacts the ground, stop moving backward and lower straight down. This creates a repeatable setup based on your leg length while keeping the hips stable.

Step 3 of this reverse lunge tutorial is stabilizing the hips:

As you step backward, rotate your shoulders slightly toward the front working leg. This subtle turn helps lock the pelvis into position and limits wobbling at the hip. A small turn is enough to improve stability so you can focus on training the legs rather than fighting for balance.

Step 4 of this lunge how-to is choosing which muscles you want to target:

The angle of your torso changes the emphasis of the exercise. Keep your torso upright during a reverse lunge to place more focus on the quads. Maintain a tall posture, drop straight down, drive through the front foot, and return to full hip extension.

If you hinge forward slightly at the hips, you create more of a sprinter lunge position. This increases the loading on the glutes and hamstrings. The lean should come from the hips rather than rounding the lower back. The right torso angle depends on whether you want to emphasize the anterior or posterior chain.

Step 5 of this lunge form breakdown is selecting the right weight:

The way you load the exercise should match your torso position. For a glute and hamstring focused lunge with a forward lean, dumbbells held at your sides are a great choice. They let you hinge without forcing the weight away from your body or stressing your lower back.

For a more upright, quad focused lunge, you can use dumbbells, a barbell across your back, or a weight held in a goblet position. The implement should support the mechanics of the variation instead of fighting against them.

Step 6 of this lunge tutorial is knowing how deep to go:

A full-depth lunge allows the back knee to descend toward the floor while the front foot stays planted and the torso remains controlled. The back knee can lightly touch, or kiss, the ground, but it should never crash into it. Control the descent and use the contact only as a depth reference.

Your range of motion may be limited by your hips, calves, Achilles tendon, or ankle mobility. If tightness prevents you from reaching the floor without losing position, stop at the deepest range you can control. Do not pitch your torso forward just to look like you reached greater depth. Work within the mobility you have and improve it over time.

Now that you know how to do lunges correctly, you can build stronger legs while avoiding the mistakes that commonly lead to knee pain and poor balance. Step backward and slightly outward, control the descent, choose the right torso angle.
